thorin.title: The Cask-Mender
paragraphs: The Caskmends were never the clan on the statues. They were the clan in the cellar  coopers and brewers in the stone-deep dark of Ironforge, mending the casks that held what other dwarves celebrated with. But trades die the way casks fail: slowly, at the seams. Sons went to the war and the engine-shops, daughters married into louder names, and the Caskmend mark faded off the cellar doors one winter at a time. By Thorin's day, the plain fact of it was this: there were no Caskmends selling in Ironforge anymore. The name had died out  and Thorin, ordinary at the family trade and entirely happy being so, found that was the one thing he couldn't be content about.

So he made a plan, the way his family made anything: without fuss, and built to last. He would revive the name  not as coopers this time, but as an alchemy house. A Caskmend brew, sold under the old mark, in cities the family never reached. Only, a man can't brew the world from one mountain's slopes. He needed the herbs of other valleys, other continents  and the recipes other peoples keep.

That's why the road, and why Coldridge Valley: a Caskmend starts at the beginning, properly, with his pack on his back like any lad setting out. What he had for the gathering was the listening  as a boy sent up the slopes for brewers' herbs he'd come home late with a full basket and no good explanation, having stood in the wind above the snowline hearing something in it that wasn't weather. The elements weren't calling him anywhere grand. They were, near as he could ever put it, asking after the place  and a Caskmend answers when something asks after the house. A cooper's patience became a healer's besides: Thorin mends people the way his family mended casks, find the failing seam and shore it kindly. And because he is a Caskmend to the bone, he still tastes the family work before anything serious  a brew before a battle is house tradition, ale or strong tea as the hour demands, and the whole guild has learned that any bottle worth keeping travels to Thorin's pack in the end.

When new companies began forming  the Lament of the Fallen among them  he joined without ceremony. Good company for the road, and a revival travels further with friends. Every herb learned and every brew mastered is one more board in the rebuilt name.
The mending is the point. The name is the work.

facts.Quirk: A brew before every battle  ale or strong tea. All the guild's alcohol finds its way to his pack.

sorinis.title: Keeper of the Tally
paragraphs: Sorinis Starhollow is young, as his people count years  and he is head of his family anyway. The -inis line is an old one among the Night Elves, every name in it ending the same way, as if the family signs its work even on its children; when the headship came to Sorinis early, he took it up the way he takes up everything: completely, and with the count kept. A druid sage and patriarch both, he tends the whole line  down to a certain Skyborne cousin whose great solo wanderings will be reported back to Sorinis, as all family counts are.

Where other druids preach the balance and then buy their boots in Darnassus, Sorinis took up the knife and the needle himself: the beast that feeds the grove should also clothe it, and a healer who cannot work a hide has understood only half of what a life is for. He is, by his own cheerful account, very good at both halves. What he wears, he made  every leather piece on his back came off his own bench, from a beast his own knife opened. It is the closest thing Sorinis has to a boast, and he makes it silently, by standing there.

His pride is not in titles. It is in the tally  a long count he has kept since his first season: every skin taken clean, every piece finished and named for its wearer, every grove left taller than he found it, every family member accounted for and thriving. Ask him what he has done and he will not gesture at the world in general. He will tell you the number, and the number will be right.

That is why the road, and why Shadowglen  and it is not, at bottom, about the hides, though there are hides in the world he has never worked and his knife knows it. It is about the line. More of the -inis family will step into the world in time  that is not a hope, it is simply the family's future arriving on schedule  and every one of them will need a head who has been there: who knows which roads are kind, which forests are honest, which waters are safe to drink and which bargains are not. So the patriarch goes first. Sorinis walks the world to understand it, tallying not only skins and groves but the world itself, so that when the next -inis stands where he stood in Shadowglen, Sorinis can assist them with knowledge instead of comfort. When the companies began forming  the Lament of the Fallen among them  he joined with his tally open at a fresh page. He intends to be able to show his work: a guild outfitted in leather he cut, a family guided into lands their line has never touched by a head who learned those lands himself, and a count at the end of it that needs no embroidery.
The work speaks. He just makes sure it's quoted correctly.

facts.Quirk: Skins every beast he passes  and wears only his own leatherwork.

malavus.title: Keeper of the Fine Print
paragraphs: The Blackwells of Stormwind were tailors  good ones, the kind whose coats outlived their wearers  and like many good houses they had a second trade conducted quietly, in the back, for customers who paid in things other than coin: the mending of arrangements. Debts refinanced. Signatures witnessed. Small dark problems made to go away neatly, the way a good tailor makes a seam disappear. Malavus grew up in the back of that shop, learning both trades at once: how to fit a coat, and how to read a contract for the clause that eats you.

What the Blackwells never had was a protector. Weavers and feeble mages, all of them  a house that could clothe a king and not defend a doorstep. So when Malavus was young, he went looking for the power his family lacked, and he knew exactly where to shop for it. The demons' contracts delighted him  they still do: literature with teeth, every clause load-bearing. He read his three times before he signed it, and improved two clauses, which the other party has never quite forgiven. He signed for protection, that a house of weavers might have one defender who is neither weaver nor feeble. And he signed for knowledge: the tailoring world whispers about felcloth, cloth worked through with fel, and Malavus holds the craftsman's view that to work a material you must understand it  and to understand fel, there is no better way than to become a little fel yourself. The interest accrues. He does not complain. A bargain is a bargain, and his  he will tell you, with some pride  was a good one. He checked.

That is why Northshire, and why the road: power is leverage, and Malavus intends to be holding a great deal of it when his own terms next come up for discussion. In the meantime he does the work properly. He clothes the guild in cloth his own hands enchanted  every stitch a small obligation of care he would deny incurring  and when the Lament of the Fallen was founded, it was Malavus who drafted the charter, because a company of friends deserves better fine print than most companies get. They made him guild master for it, which he accepted with the air of a man signing something he has already read twice.
If there is a warmer reason he gathers good people around him against the day his bill comes due, he has never entered it in any ledger. Some accounts a man keeps only in the original.

facts.Guild: Guild Master, Lament of the Fallen
facts.Quirk: The Staff Meeting  he consults each demon before a serious fight, and apologises in writing to any who fall.

skyrinis.title: The Patriarch's Hero
paragraphs: Until recently, Skyrinis Starhollow's family was a rumour in somebody else's records. The Skyborne branch of the -inis line had been sundered from the Night Elf clan for longer than either side could properly account  long enough that the kinship, when a lineage check finally established it, arrived as news: the sky elves were family. On paper, the matter was settled. But Skyrinis understands what paper is worth in a family. A name restored to the records is not the same as a branch restored to standing  and the wider clan, polite as it is, is watching to see what the new relations are for.

Sorinis received them as kin  warmly, deliberately. The patriarch wants elves standing tall in the world, and he is clear-eyed about the arithmetic: a Skyborne hero lifts the sky elves, and the sky elves, gathered under the -inis name, lift the whole clan. So when the Skyborne hopefuls volunteered for the proving, Sorinis came himself to choose  and chose Skyrinis: the youngest of the branch, the brightest-eyed, his hero out of their line. Friendship is his method, never pressure; a patriarch who means to build a cornerstone does not start by leaning on it. Skyrinis, for his part, knows he was picked, and intends to make the picking look wise. The great Journey is his proving. He will walk the whole world, zone by zone, and gather everything  every herb and ore the clan's crafts might need, every recipe, every weapon and curiosity worth the keeping  and lay it all at the family's feet, with the counts kept clean and reported to the patriarch as he goes. If the Skyborne branch's first gift to the -inis line is the entire world, itemised, let anyone call them the poor relations afterwards.
So he starts where his people start, on Zephras Isle, with an empty pack, a cousin's example, and a list with the whole world on it. The Journey is long. He wouldn't shorten it by a single item.
For the clan. All of it, for the clan.

facts.Quirk: The Offering  no node passes unharvested, and the finest find of every expedition goes to Sorinis.
